classified_risks.risk: Lead cadence collapses into the slower color-cycle cadence and breaks macro-round pacing.
classified_risks.evidence_required: Independent batch cursors, same-boundary ordering tests, and Save/Restore exact-once tests.
classified_risks.human_question: Can players understand when lead influence changes without a public identity reveal?

classified_risks.risk: AI acts without a private fact legally available to the equivalent human seat.
classified_risks.evidence_required: Player/AI semantic parity tests and zero exposure of rival lead or hidden order.
classified_risks.human_question: Does AI behavior feel coherent without appearing to know another player's secret?

classified_risks.risk: Immediate replacement activation permits repeated commodity claims in one track revision.
classified_risks.evidence_required: Exact-once input matrix, eight-player concurrency, and locked replacement Save/Restore.
classified_risks.human_question: Is the incoming-locked state obvious without slowing track scanning?

classified_risks.risk: Optional merges can reduce the normal deck below the size needed to draw to five.
classified_risks.evidence_required: All-zone card counting, rejection Receipt, and maintenance termination tests.
classified_risks.human_question: Does the rejection clearly communicate why a seemingly valid merge is blocked?

classified_risks.risk: Higher-level track spawns bypass merge progression and make acquisition outcomes swingy.
classified_risks.evidence_required: Zero high-level track spawn tests for both normal and commodity supplies.
classified_risks.human_question: Does level-one-only supply make early track choices varied enough?

classified_risks.risk: A post-lock commodity can mutate an immutable current batch or be unusably ambiguous.
classified_risks.evidence_required: Availability-batch persistence and current/next batch legality tests.
classified_risks.human_question: Can players predict current-versus-next availability at a glance?

classified_risks.risk: Invalid prebound targets produce undefined refunds, destinations, or reselection behavior.
classified_risks.evidence_required: Typed policy coverage for every action and deterministic Receipt tests.
classified_risks.human_question: Does a full-refund fizzle feel fair when the action slot and card are still spent?

classified_risks.risk: Players may treat mathematically inferred lead identity as a privacy defect or as excessive bookkeeping.
classified_risks.evidence_required: Lead inference unique-rate simulation and public-cue audits.
classified_risks.human_question: Is inference satisfying deduction, irrelevant noise, or too deterministic?

classified_risks.risk: One starting asset per color can produce blocked openings; two can erase early scarcity.
classified_risks.evidence_required: Opening chain timing, zero-asset block rate, and first-batch choice counts by player count.
classified_risks.human_question: Does the opening feel constrained in an interesting way rather than stalled?

classified_risks.risk: Track ratio can starve DBG growth or commodity merging, especially at six and eight players.
classified_risks.evidence_required: Normal purchase-to-draw and commodity Level II/III timing distributions.
classified_risks.human_question: Does the mixed track offer meaningful tension without frequent dead arrivals?

classified_risks.risk: No cap permits color dominance; a 12 percent cap may flatten coordinated influence.
classified_risks.evidence_required: Color min/max, cap-hit rate, and lead acquisition advantage by roster size.
classified_risks.human_question: Can players feel their stance matter without one coalition locking a color?

classified_risks.risk: Uncapped per-batch refresh creates overflow while a cap of three may block expensive plans.
classified_risks.evidence_required: Per-color overflow and zero-asset blocked-action rates.
classified_risks.human_question: Is the refresh cap legible and does it reward planning rather than hoarding?

classified_risks.risk: Twenty-second maintenance drags; eight seconds may punish comprehension and accessibility.
classified_risks.evidence_required: Maintenance timeout and optional-merge acceptance rates by experience level.
classified_risks.human_question: Can first-time players inspect a merge choice comfortably within eight seconds?

classified_risks.risk: One-batch lead tenure may feel noisy; two batches may amplify acquisition advantage and end-tail length.
classified_risks.evidence_required: Lead advantage, macro-round duration, inference rate, and victory-pending tail by player count.
classified_risks.human_question: Which cadence gives enough time to plan without making the hidden order obvious?

cross_cutting_verification_controls.human_question: Does summary presentation remain understandable at the eight-player action ceiling?
Does the 2x solar advantage read as a strategic opportunity without requiring formula tracking?
